about: Conformance vectors for SNO (Simple Nostr Objects). Every `expected` was produced by decks/sno-reference.py; run decks/sno-vectors.py to check that they still agree. DECK-0003 §9.1 says how to use them.

conventions.event: The event to read. Real events are copied from relays as published, signature included. Synthetic events are unsigned (no `sig`) and carry their NIP-01 `id`; their author is a placeholder with no key behind it. These vectors test the object, not the signature.
conventions.palette_event: Present when the payload names a palette by nevent or naddr: the event a reader fetched for it. Absent means the fetch failed or was not attempted.
conventions.strict: true: a conformant reader MUST give this result. false: the spec leaves room, or is unclear, and `note` says how; the result shown is the reference's.
conventions.detail: "summary": `expected` carries counts rather than per-vertex arrays, to keep this file small.
conventions.expected.valid: false: a reader MUST NOT render the object. `rule` names the §1.9 rule the reference cited; `error` is its message, which is informative and need not match word for word.
conventions.expected.status: "object": a payload was read. "hidden": a kind 33331 sealed to a place (§3.4). "default-avatar": a kind 11333 with empty content (§3.3).
conventions.expected.positions_ticks: Each position in whole ticks, 120 to a model unit, in the frame of §2: a v1 payload's Z is already negated.
conventions.expected.positions: The same positions in model units, as exact fractions written "n" or "n/d".
conventions.expected.colors: One per vertex. color_form "palette": the palette entry as three integers 0..255. color_form "literal": a v1 triple, clamped to 0..1.
conventions.expected.face_colors: null when every face interpolates its corners; otherwise one palette entry per face (§1.4a).
conventions.expected.fronts: One per face: (b - a) x (c - a) on positions_ticks, in square ticks (§1.4). Only the direction matters; the zero vector means the face has no front.
conventions.expected.parts: As written, eight integers each, in the frame of §2 (§1.10).

vectors.description: The worked example of Appendix A in canonical form: four vertices, four faces wound outward, built-in palette.
Appendix A with `ticks` written as [-4]: four whole remainders run-length encoded. Not canonical, and a reader MUST accept it.
Appendix A with every remainder written out as [0, 0, 0]. Not canonical, and a reader MUST accept it.
No vertices, no colors, no faces: valid, and draws nothing.
Sub-unit positions: 40 ticks is exactly one third. A negative position is the floor in `vertices` plus a non-negative remainder, so -1/3 is [-1] and 80 ticks.
Mode `points` with no faces: a point cloud.
Mode `lines` with no faces: one polyline through the vertices in order.
Mode `lines` with faces: the edges of the faces, each drawn once.
The largest `unit`.
A legacy `type` field on a v2 payload, with a value that is not even a string. Ignored, never rejected on.
A field this version does not define. Ignored, not rejected.
`v` written as 2.0. Every JSON reader sees the number 2.
A vertex at 9 units with no declared extent: the default of 8 grows to 9.
A vertex at 8 units and 1 tick: it needs an extent of 9.
A vertex at -8 1/120 units, written as the floor [-9] and a remainder of 119 ticks: it needs an extent of 9.
A declared extent of 12 that already contains the data is kept.
An extent of 0 is out of range and becomes 8.
An extent of 65 is out of range and becomes 8.
An extent that is not an integer becomes 8. Never a rejection.
A vertex 100 units out, past the 64-unit bound a publisher MUST NOT cross. The reference repairs the extent to 100.
vectors.note: §1.8 lets a reader either reject this payload or repair it. The reference repairs; a reader that rejects is also conformant.

vectors.description: Standing on the Earth, facing east.
`up` false means the same as absent.
`spin` without `up`: checked, then ignored.
A version 1 payload: Z is negated on read, colors are literal triples clamped to 0..1, and the legacy `type` is ignored. 1.5 clamps to 1 and -0.25 to 0.
A version 1 payload with sub-unit positions: the Z negation applies to the whole position, ticks included, so 1/3 in Z reads as -1/3.
A v1 payload with `facecolors`. Face colors are indices whatever the version, read against the built-in.
The built-in palette named explicitly.
Indices 0 and 255, the two ends of the built-in.
A palette carried in the object, four entries, as in Appendix A's second example.
The shortest palette an object may carry: two entries.
The longest palette an object may carry: 256 entries.
A palette named by nevent, fetched: a live kind 3367 color moment with four `c` tags in uppercase hex. Index n is the nth `c` tag.
The same object when the palette event could not be fetched: the built-in stands in, so index 3 is the built-in's 3. Never a rejection.
A fetched palette event with no `c` tags and a JSON array in `content`: the legacy form, read second.
A fetched event with both `c` tags and a content palette: the tags win.
A fetched event that is not a palette (one `c` tag and an emoji): a failed fetch, so the built-in.
A fetched event whose second `c` tag is not #rrggbb: the whole tag path fails, the content is not a palette, so the built-in.
A palette named by naddr and not fetched: the built-in.
`facecolors` [238, -3]: four flat red faces.
`facecolors` [238, 235, -1, 239]: a run in the middle repeats the index before it.
`facecolors` of index 0 is a color, not absence: every face is filled with index 0.
Face colors read against a palette the object carries.
`facecolors` [] on an object with no faces expands to exactly one index per face, which is none.
One triangle in the XY plane, corners counter-clockwise seen from +Z: its front looks toward the viewer, +Z.
The same triangle with two corners swapped: its front looks away, -Z. A reader MUST still draw both sides.
The same triangle written starting from a different corner, [1, 2, 0]: a rotation of the indices keeps the front.
A v1 triangle in the XZ plane. v2 with these numbers looks down (-Y); the v1 Z negation is a mirror, so the v1 front looks up (+Y). No reversal of the indices is applied.
The v2 twin of the previous vector: the same numbers, and the front looks down (-Y).
An open sheet of two triangles, one looking +Y and one -Y. A reader takes each front from its winding and MUST NOT infer or unify them.
A triangle whose corners are a third of a unit apart: the front is exact in ticks.
Three distinct vertices on one line: valid under rule 8, zero area, and no front (the zero vector).
Two distinct vertex indices at the same position: valid, and the face has no front.
One `a` and one `e` reference, the first with a relay hint, placed three times: whole and sub-unit offsets, a quarter turn, a half scale and a double scale.
Placements at exactly +7680 and -7680 ticks, the 64-unit bound.
A scale step of -90. Whether the placed object's unit stays in 0..84 is known only once it is fetched; out of range it is a placeholder, so the parent is valid.
An object with no vertices of its own, only placements: rule 13.
`refs` with no `parts`: nothing is placed, and that is not an error.
A reference whose relay hint is an empty string: still three strings.
An `a` reference whose `d` is empty, which NIP-01 allows.
A bag item, kind 3330, unsigned, with the payload in `content`.
An avatar, kind 11333, carrying a payload.
An avatar with empty content: the default avatar, not an error.
A kind 33331 sealed to a place: an `encrypted` tag, and a preview sentence in `content`. Not parsed as a payload and not an error.

vectors.description: A kind 33331 with no `d` tag. The reference reads the payload.
vectors.note: §3.1 requires a publisher to write `d`, but does not say whether a reader refuses an event without one. sno-core's feed drops it; the reference reads it.

vectors.description: A payload with no `name`. The reference accepts it.
vectors.note: §1.1 marks `name` required and says a reader MUST reject a payload missing a required field, but §1.9 never checks `name` and neither does the reference. Open question for the spec.

vectors.description: A name of 100 characters. A reader truncates it to 64 for display; it is never a rejection.
A live object: arkinox's Triforce, built in snocrash, the one Ditto's Blobbi showed as furniture.
A live version 1 object with a legacy `type` and sub-unit ticks.
A live object with geometry of its own and placements.

vectors.description: A v2 payload whose colors are triples, as written for a few weeks before 2026-09-16. The reference rejects it under rule 8b.
vectors.note: §5 lets a reader reject this payload or read the triples literally. The reference rejects; sno-core and Grimoire read them.

vectors.description: `unit` written as 0.0. The reference, reading JSON in Python, sees a float and rejects under rule 5.
vectors.note: JSON has one number type. JavaScript's JSON.parse cannot tell 0.0 from 0, so sno-core and Grimoire accept this; Python's json module can, so the reference rejects. Open question for the spec: whether an integer field may be written with a fractional part of zero.
